videos.t: How to Make an Arduino WebSocket Server with an ESP32
videos.desc:
The WebSocket protocol is a useful tool for communicating between servers and clients without the need for HTTP. Here, I show how to create an Arduino WebSocket server on an ESP32 that echoes simple text messages back to connected clients. I test the server with a basic Python script.

Arduino and Python code from the video can be found here: http://shawnhymel.com/1675/arduino-websocket-server-using-an-esp32/

videos.t: How to Create a Web Server (with WebSockets) Using an ESP32 in Arduino
videos.desc:
This is a continuation of the ESP32 WebSocket Server video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZbX-l1Dl4N4. Let's take it to the next level! We begin by hosting a web server and WebSocket server on an ESP32 using Arduino. Next, we use SPIFFS to upload a simple index.html page that we write separately. This page will open a WebSocket connection back to the ESP32, where we can use the page's button to toggle an LED (relatively quickly).

videos.t: Hack a Pumpkin: Spoopy Poopy, the Gaseous Gourd
videos.desc:
Here is my official entry to Tech-nic-Allie's #HackAPumpkin challenge: Spoopy Poopy, the Farting Pumpkin. I can disgust those Trick-or-Treaters with this wonderfully flatulent trick--now with fart-flavored fragrance! A passive infrared (PIR) sensor detects the presence of warm bodies and triggers the whole fart sequence. An Adafruit Feather M0 Express running #CircuitPython controls the lights (NeoPixels) and plays an audio clip out through pin A0. The fog machine is a vape pen loaded with hal

videos.t: Getting Started with Mozilla WebThings Part 1: Setup on a Raspberry Pi
videos.desc:
Mozilla (the makers of Firefox) have created a custom Internet of Things (IoT) hub that can run on a single-board computer (SBC). In this tutorial, I show you how to install the WebThings gateway on a Raspberry Pi and then control  smart plug using your smart phone.

On the next episode, we'll create a custom IoT device using Arduino and an ESP8266 device that can communicate with the WebThings gateway server.

References:
Mozilla WebThings: https://iot.mozilla.org/
Web of Things standard: https://www.w3.org/WoT/

videos.t: Getting Started with Mozilla WebThings Part 2: Building an ESP8266 Temperature Sensor with Arduino
videos.desc:
In the last episode (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WHite8vdcbE), I showed you how to set up the Mozilla WebThings project on a Raspberry Pi and toggle a simple smart plug. This time, we dig even deeper and build our own IoT device with Arduino on an ESP8266.

The ESP8266 is connected to a digital temperature sensor, which we can query using the I2C protocol. We then use the WebThings library for Arduino to construct a request that automatically updates the displayed temperature value in the WebThings interface.

Arduino code: https://gist.github.com/ShawnHymel/327f9fc4cc57594e4f482b868be02e9

videos.t: Keysight DSOX1204G Oscilloscope Review
videos.desc:
The Keysight DSOX1204G is a 4-channel oscilloscope with 70-200 MHz bandwidth (depending on the options selected). It is one of Keysight's entry-level scopes and could be a great addition to any professional engineer's workbench or for universities. However, it is more expensive than most other entry-level oscilloscopes, as you're paying for the Keysight name and customer support.

In the video, I cover some of the oscilloscope's features, talk about what it might be used for, and give my opinions on it. Considering it is an entry-level oscilloscope, I compare it to 2 other entry-level oscillos

videos.t: Custom Wake Word Part 1: Capturing Data | TinyML
videos.desc:
Welcome to the first part in my series on creating a custom wake word for Edge AI and TinyML! I'll be working through a longer project to create a machine learning model that can be deployed on single board computers (e.g. Raspberry Pi) and microcontrollers (e.g. Arduino). We will train this model to recognize one or more key phrases, known as "wake words" or "hotwords." You probably recognize common wake words such as "Alexa," "Hey Siri," and "OK Google."

videos.t: Custom Wake Word Part 2: Curating Data | TinyML
videos.desc:

videos.t: Wio Terminal TinyML - Speech Recognition
videos.desc:
The Wio Terminal is a development platform by Seeed Studio (https://www.seeedstudio.com/Wio-Terminal-p-4509.html). It combines a SAMD51 microcontroller with Bluetooth/WiFi connectivity, various sensors, an LED screen, a buzzer, and some buttons. While it makes for a fine IoT development kit, I wanted to see how well it would run embedded machine learning applications (TinyML). Specifically, I wanted to test its ability to handle speech recognition (or more specifically, keyword spotting).

Disclosure: Seeed Studio sent me a Wio Terminal to play with and create a video about.

videos.t: ESP32 - Kconfig with ESP-IDF Tutorial
videos.desc:
In this video, I’ll show you how to use Kconfig with ESP-IDF to make your ESP32 projects configurable and easier to maintain. Kconfig is the system behind the familiar idf.py menuconfig tool, allowing you to enable or disable features, set parameters, and even create your own configuration options without manually editing source files.

videos.t: ESP32 - I2C with ESP-IDF Tutorial
videos.desc:
In this video, I’ll show you how to use I2C communication in ESP-IDF to read temperature data from the TMP102 sensor. This tutorial covers the fundamentals of the I2C protocol, how to configure ESP-IDF's I2C master driver, and how to properly read and convert temperature data from a real sensor. 

If you would like to go further, check out my full IoT Firmware Development with ESP32 and ESP-IDF course: https://learnembedded.dev/courses/iot-firmware-development-with-esp32-and-esp-idf/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=esp32_iot_course_evergreen

videos.t: ESP32 - WiFi Driver with ESP-IDF Tutorial
videos.desc:
Learn how to build a robust WiFi driver for ESP32 using ESP-IDF from scratch. This tutorial breaks down the ESP-IDF WiFi stack into its core building blocks, showing you how to create a custom component that handles station mode connections, event-driven callbacks, and DHCP for both IPv4 and IPv6. Unlike simplified examples that use convenience functions, we'll implement the network interface, driver attachment, and event handlers step-by-step so you understand exactly what's happening under the hood.

If you would like to go further, check out my full IoT Firmware Development with ESP32 and E

videos.t: ESP32 - HTTP GET with ESP-IDF Tutorial
videos.desc:
Learn how to make HTTP GET requests from an ESP32 microcontroller using ESP-IDF and low-level BSD sockets in this comprehensive tutorial. We'll start with the fundamentals of HTTP communication and socket programming, then build a complete application that connects to WiFi, performs DNS lookups, establishes socket connections, sends HTTP requests, and processes server responses. This hands-on project will give you the essential networking skills needed to build IoT devices that communicate with web servers and REST APIs.

videos.t: What is Transport Layer Security (TLS)?
videos.desc:
In this video, I’ll explain what Transport Layer Security (TLS) is, how it relates to Secure Sockets Layer (SSL), and how it keeps our internet communications safe. We’ll look at how encryption, authentication, and digital certificates work together to ensure that the data we send stays private, unaltered, and verified (whether you’re browsing a website or connecting an IoT device to the cloud).

We’ll start by reviewing the problems with unencrypted communication and symmetric key exchange, then explore how asymmetric cryptography, certificate authorities, and the TLS handshake solve those is

videos.t: What is MQTT?
videos.desc:
MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport) is a lightweight, publish/subscribe messaging protocol designed for low-power, low-bandwidth, or unreliable networks. From the early days of monitoring oil pipelines over satellite links to today’s massive IoT deployments, MQTT has evolved into a flexible and powerful messaging system used around the world.

You can find a written version of this overview here: https://shawnhymel.com/3046/what-is-mqtt-an-introduction-to-the-lightweight-iot-messaging-protocol/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=esp32_iot_course_evergreen

videos.t: Getting Started with the Mosquitto MQTT Broker (with SSL/TLS)
videos.desc:
In this video, we show how to configure and use Mosquitto, one of the most widely adopted open-source MQTT brokers. Mosquitto is lightweight, easy to install, and maintained by the Eclipse Foundation. While it doesn’t include dashboards or databases like full-featured IoT platforms, it provides a solid, minimal broker that you can extend however you like, which is perfect for prototyping or building a self-hosted IoT system from scratch. Because it’s small and reliable, Mosquitto is a great option for developers running local servers, lab setups, or containerized deployments.

videos.t: Interview with Sid Deliwala (ECEDHA 2026): Teaching Edge AI from Day One
videos.desc:
In this interview from the ECEDHA 2026 conference, I spoke with Professor Siddharth Deliwala from the University of Pennsylvania about how he’s introducing edge AI concepts to students as early as their freshman year. Instead of waiting for advanced coursework, his approach focuses on top-down, project-based learning by getting students to build real systems with hardware, software, and networking components from the start.

videos.t: Interview with Omiya Hassan (ECEDHA 2026): Preparing Students for Edge AI
videos.desc:
In this interview from the ECEDHA 2026 conference, I spoke with Omiya Hassan, Assistant Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Boise State University, about how edge AI is being taught from both the software and hardware perspectives. We discuss the growing need for ECE students to understand machine learning fundamentals, as well as the equally important need for computer science students to understand the hardware their models run on.

A big theme in this conversation is bridging the gap between disciplines. Omiya shares how she structures her edge AI course to pair CS and ECE s

videos.t: Interview with Mario Simoni (ECEDHA 2026): AI in Engineering Education
videos.desc:
In this interview from the 2026 ECEDHA conference, I spoke with Mario Simoni, Department Head of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Rose-Hulman, about how AI is being integrated into engineering education. We discuss where AI naturally fits within ECE (like control systems, embedded systems, and resource-constrained environments), as well as the growing importance of understanding how to deploy machine learning on real hardware rather than relying on the cloud.

videos.t: Domain randomization is a powerful technique #Arduino #robotics #engineering #education #AI #ML
Training a balance bot with reinforcement learning
videos.desc:
Meet my new robot, Aiden 🤖 I wanted to explore how to use #ReinforcementLearning to tackle an old balance bot problem. Simulating the bot was pretty simple. Training the #AI and deploying it to real hardware was another thing entirely. The fun part is seeing how an AI control system responds when the real world gets messy. The sim2real gap is real and really tricky! More testing, tuning, and probably a few crashes ahead.
